note: Adapted from Holmgren 1910 (German). The original is a redescription of a series of Madagascar specimens following Wasmann's 1897 original description, not the original description of 1897; it states explicitly that the soldier of Coptotermes truncatus was described by Wasmann, and what is recorded here is the supplementary description and measurements of soldiers collected later. The same work, biostor-184507, only lists the species in a catalogue and gives no description.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Soldier body length 4—6 mm, rather variable, two size classes of soldier can be distinguished, but there are no other differences between them. Head with mandibles about 2.3 mm long, or 1.9—2 mm; head width 1.2 mm (the original records Sjöstedt's means as body length 5, head with mandibles 2, head width 1.2 mm). Antennae 15-segmented: segment 2 about as long as segment 3 but distinctly thicker, segment 4 slightly shorter than segment 3. Frontal tube short; the clypeal region is extremely compressed at the middle by the development of the frontal tube and is therefore very short, but extends slightly backwards on both sides to the mandibular articulations; the transparent apical area of the clypeus is rather short but still clearly visible. The antennal spots on the transverse band are fairly distinct; the antennal sockets are lateral on the head and are covered from above by the slightly raised antennal ridges. The sides of the head in front of the antennae run parallel to accommodate the outer articular processes of the mandibles. The dorsal surface of the frontal tube is covered with concentric chitinous rings.
